entity.name: openSUSE India - Bengaluru Connect 2027 Organizing Team
entity.description:
We are the organizing team for openSUSE India - Bengaluru Connect 2027: Divyanshu Prakash, Dushyant Acharya and Rithull Raj Kallat. The event is planned for two consecutive days in January 2027 at Newton School of Technology, Bengaluru, in collaboration with the college. Exact dates and overnight permission remain to be confirmed. Participation is capped at 250, with 30 staff/support separately catered. The college provides the venue, internet and basic facilities at no cash cost, as advised by the organizers.

The program combines three 30-minute Linux/openSUSE talks, parallel Starter Lab and Idea Lab sessions, a 20-hour Geeko Buildathon (Day 1 2:30 PM to Day 2 10:30 AM), a QR-based Geeko Quest, optional Rookie/Expert Midnight Bug Hunt, four Arcade games and a Demo Arena for every submitting team. Six finalists pitch on stage. Tracks are Terminal Titans, Root Access, GeekoOps, Desktop Reboot, Upstream Heroes, and What Does Linux Need Next?

We seek FOSS United event support and community collaboration to introduce students to Linux, encourage useful FOSS contributions and connect new contributors with the wider community. We also plan to seek sponsorship from openSUSE. FOSS United and openSUSE are prospective partners; no sponsorship is confirmed.

projects.name: openSUSE India - Bengaluru Connect 2027
projects.description:
Two-day Linux/FOSS community event planned for January 2027 at Newton School of Technology, Bengaluru, in collaboration with the college. Exact dates and overnight permissions remain pending. Cap: 250 participants plus 30 staff/support. College venue, internet and basic facilities are provided at no cash cost.

Three 30-minute talks, parallel Starter Lab and Idea Lab, and a 20-hour Buildathon (Day 1 2:30 PM to Day 2 10:30 AM). Six tracks: Terminal Titans, Root Access, GeekoOps, Desktop Reboot, Upstream Heroes, and What Does Linux Need Next? Optional QR Quest, individual Rookie/Expert Bug Hunt and four Arcade games complement an expo for every team and six stage finalists.

Cash budget: catering INR 120400; operations/rewards INR 64000, including 25 reward T-shirts at INR 300 = INR 7500; conditional cash prizes INR 50000 (25000/15000/10000). Direct costs INR 234400; 10% contingency INR 23440; total INR 257840. Rates are estimates, not quotes. We request INR 50000 from FOSS United for catering; remaining gap after receipt INR 207840. We also plan to approach openSUSE and other sponsors. No cash sponsorship is confirmed. All planned expenses precede future funding offsets; in-kind goods will reduce matching cash costs without double counting.

Targets: 100 Starter Lab completions, 60+ valid submissions and 10 upstream/community-useful follow-ups. We propose public repositories, valid FOSS licenses, attribution and reproducible demos, with FOSS United rule alignment to be discussed. No website software license is asserted. Participants retain their project licenses. We plan an opt-in project directory, an expense/outcome report within 14 days and contributor follow-up within 30 days. Partnership and overnight access are not claimed as confirmed.
